subject: Avatech vendor evaluation: test plan, unit-economics & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mark Hsu <mark.hsu@avatech.com>, Laila Gomez <laila.gomez@avatech.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Avatech vendor evaluation: test plan, unit-economics & next steps

Hi Mark / Laila —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary objective: reduce inference unit cost for customer-facing chat (support triage) while keeping p99 latency < 400ms for short queries (~64 tokens).
- Monthly steady-state: ~3-4M tokens/day (burst to ~10M/day during business hours).
- Compliance constraints: need KMS integration and an audit log for any private VPC deployment.

What Redwood will run for the evaluation (attached test plan + cost workbook):
1) Per-1M-token cost comparison vs two hyperscaler endpoint configs (baseline and optimized) — measure billed tokens and raw compute cost.
2) Batch sizing sweep (batch=1,4,8,16) with latency/throughput curves (p50/p95/p99) for the primary prompt distribution you sent.
3) Prefix/KV caching experiment to measure effective cache-hit improvement and token savings for 30-day session replay patterns.
4) End-to-end quality check: sample 200 prompts across ticket categories to ensure no regression vs your current model.

Immediate asks from your side (can you confirm by EOD Tuesday?):
- A sample workload file (tokenized) or an export of ~2,000 representative prompts (we can take a sanitized copy).
- Expected SLA or latency threshold you'd consider acceptable for production (you mentioned 400ms p99 as a target).
- Procurement contact for kickoffs / PO timeline (if you want Redwood to prepare an MSA/quote).

Attachments: avatech_tokenized_costs.xlsx (template I filled with placeholders), redwood_vs_hyperscaler-test-plan.pdf

Proposed schedule: kickoff tests Wed 10/21, 3 business days for batch runs + cost analysis, then a short demo of results the following week. If you need faster turnaround we can prioritize the 1M-token cost sweep first.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
[Attachment: avatech_tokenized_costs.xlsx] [Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler-test-plan.pdf]

From: Mark Hsu <mark.hsu@avatech.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Avatech vendor evaluation: test plan, unit-economics & next steps

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. Quick answers below and a few notes: 

- Sample workload: attaching a sanitized sample CSV (2000 rows) in a separate email — includes category tags.
- Latency target: 400ms p99 is the right constraint for the UI path; for async features we can accept higher latency but we'd like to see cost wins first.
- Procurement: looped in procurement@avatech.com (Ana Morales) to coordinate PO timeline and MSA. They typically need 3–4 weeks for enterprise review.

Two additional items:
1) We run most inference on GCP right now but we're evaluating hosted APIs and dedicated endpoints. Can you add an explicit comparison vs Google Vertex AI (n1-high baseline + autoscale) and also vs an optimized dedicated GPU host (a single A100 profile)?
2) For the caching experiment: our session patterns have ~40% prefix-repeat behavior across 30 days according to our telemetry. If Redwood can show >20% token reduction in realistic runs, that's compelling.

Happy to sync after you get the sample CSV.

-Mark

Looping you in as requested. Stephanie (Security & Compliance) will own the KMS/HSM and audit-log questions; Lauren (Solutions) will coordinate test infra and access.

Stephanie — short summary of compliance asks from Avatech:
- KMS integration for key management (customer-managed keys preferred)
- Audit logs for request/response metadata retained for 90 days (we can discuss longer retention under enterprise add-on)
- Optional VPC deployment if required for RPO/regulatory controls

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Avatech competitive asks and test messaging

Karthik / Priyom — quick internal note to align on how we frame the results: 

Competitive angle vs hyperscalers (short bullets for demo slides):
- Consistent per-token cost at scale: our batching + KV caching reduces paid tokens vs raw hyperscaler endpoints by up to ~30% in workloads with repeat prefixes.
- Predictable latency SLOs: per-route p99 guardrails and graceful fallback to cheaper model variants when burst capacity is reached.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted API for quick onboarding, Dedicated pools for stable throughput, Private VPC for compliance — single API surface.

Suggested tests to highlight strengths (we'll run these in the plan):
- Cache hit sensitivity: synthetic replay to measure % token saved at varying prefix-repeat ratios (10/20/40/60%).
- Effective batch economics: per-1M-token cost at batch sizes (1/4/8/16) and tradeoff curves (p95 latency vs $/1M tokens).
- Fallback behavior: force a simulated capacity exhaustion and show how Redwood falls back to a lower-cost variant while preserving availability.

Ask: Priyom, can you draft a short 1-slide summary of expected TCO delta vs Vertex baseline (assume Avatech's numbers in the attached workbook) by EOD tomorrow? I can package it with a short narrative.

-Lauren

Hi all — quick update and confirmed kickoff logistics: 

1) Test kickoff scheduled Thu 10/22 09:00 PT. Redwood will spin the three experiments (Redwood hosted, Vertex API baseline, Dedicated A100 profile) against the same tokenized sample you shared. Expect an initial summary within 72 hours.

2) Access request: please create a temporary S3 bucket or provide a signed URL for the sample CSV and set read access for redwood-test@redwood.com. We only need read access to run the normalized workload.

3) Cache-hit goal: you mentioned ~40% prefix-repeat in your telemetry — our goal is to demonstrate >=20% real token savings end-to-end for the primary chat workload to make a compelling TCO story. If we hit >30% we can accelerate a pilot.

4) Procurement note: Ana, if you can share an MSA template or a PO-mock by Friday, we can scope the dedicated trial and the SOW. We can also run tests under an NDA if that speeds you up.

Links & artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/AVA-2026-0914, attached cost workbook with placeholders.

Next sync: brief check-in after the first run (Fri 10/23) to review raw numbers and pick the metric set for the executive summary.

Thanks — looking forward to results.

Best,
